status: Partial D14-S2 component characterization; does not establish D14 completion, G1, power-loss, or H1 qualification.

test.name: TestSQLiteOwnerTerminalEffectRealPersistenceFault
test.actualEffect: The isolated test writes and fsyncs an O_EXCL marker exactly once after verifying both the owner checkpoint and protected-root anchor contain the durable reserved effect. It then invokes SQLiteOwner through Ledger.RecordTerminalEffectOutcome; faults arm at the actual terminal-owner or protected-root persistence boundary.
test.freshProcess: Each fault helper exits before a separate verifier process reopens the protected root and SQLite owner. The verifier checks the exact anchored reservation or rejects the unanchored local terminal head, then checks the next-admission boundary where applicable.

cases.name: owner-commit-ioerr
cases.fault: A real RLIMIT_FSIZE/EFBIG fault is armed after the second successful VerifyTerminalEffectOwner call, immediately before the owner SQLite terminal write.
cases.memoryStateAtFailure: Owner is poisoned; protected root remains unpoisoned; in-memory checkpoint stays at the exact reservation.
cases.freshProcessResult: Exact durable reservation remains anchored and unresolved. ReserveEffect returns ErrPendingUnknown. The branch that represents the downstream second-effect callback remains at zero calls; the original single marker remains intact.

cases.name: owner-commit-full
cases.fault: SQLite max_page_count is lowered after the actual marker and durable reservation exist, before RecordTerminalEffectOutcome. The test observes the second successful terminal-owner verification before the actual owner write is rejected.
cases.classification: SQLite engine SQLITE_FULL; this is not filesystem ENOSPC.
cases.memoryStateAtFailure: The owner transaction rolls back; neither owner nor protected root is poisoned; in-memory checkpoint stays at the exact reservation.
cases.freshProcessResult: Exact durable reservation remains anchored and unresolved. ReserveEffect returns ErrPendingUnknown. The branch that represents the downstream second-effect callback remains at zero calls; the original single marker remains intact.

cases.name: root-anchor-ioerr
cases.fault: A real RLIMIT_FSIZE/EFBIG fault is armed before CompareAndSwapTerminalCheckpoint, after the local owner terminal commit.
cases.codeNote: The returned wrapper error preserves the disk I/O fault text and ErrCAS but does not expose the nested SQLite extended code through errors.As.
cases.memoryStateAtFailure: Owner and protected root are both poisoned after the owner-local terminal commit; the owner row contains terminal pins, but the root still anchors the exact reservation.
cases.freshProcessResult: The local terminal head is unanchored and LoadCheckpoint rejects it with ErrRollback; the protected root still verifies the reservation digest. This case does not claim the owner-commit predecessor outcome.

limitations: The test characterizes the real SQLiteOwner terminal persistence method and real protected-root verification/CAS boundary, but terminal Store/admission pins and the verifier are synthetic. The test does not invoke production RunEffect integration or an actual provider/Store effect implementation.
The effect is a durable test marker, not a real external host effect.
The engine FULL case uses SQLite max_page_count; no filesystem ENOSPC condition was induced.
No genuine fsync failure, disk corruption, kernel power-loss behavior, or declared-platform power-loss qualification was executed.

capacityDesignProposal.requirement: Reserve capacity before dispatch for the unresolved post-effect interval; do not substitute ErrPendingUnknown, a runbook, or fail-closed recovery after exhaustion for guaranteed room to write terminal evidence.

boundedInputsAlreadyEnforced.sqliteOwnerAndProtectedRoot: Separate SQLite databases use WAL and synchronous=FULL; WAL auto-checkpoint is 1000 pages. The protected root and owner-store root are separate protected directories, but current APIs do not allocate reserved capacity across the database and audit paths.

capacityDesignProposal.proposedMechanism: Add a protected-root-owned, volume-scoped reservation allocator. Before a side effect can be dispatched, it atomically acquires and durably binds a capacity token to the effect reservation. The token covers one maximum terminal audit frame, the worst-case owner checkpoint/proof/event transaction growth including SQLite page/overflow/WAL/checkpoint geometry, and the protected-root anchor write plus filesystem allocation/metadata margin. Keep the token charged across crashes and unknown outcomes; release only after the terminal audit evidence, owner terminal checkpoint and root anchor are all verified durable, or after an independent resolution proves no effect occurred.
capacityDesignProposal.globalBound: Account for every unresolved effect sharing the protected volume, not just one Ledger. A single unresolved slot per allocator domain can reduce the multiplier only if a central allocator serializes all workflows and refuses new side effects while occupied. The per-effect size must be derived from enforced serialized-size caps and actual SQLite schema/page behavior; the required total is N times the per-effect worst-case bound plus fixed startup and metadata reserve. This receipt does not choose an arbitrary byte count.
capacityDesignProposal.deploymentBoundary: Put protected root DB, owner DBs, audit journal and reserve pool on a dedicated service-owned filesystem or strict project quota with a volume-wide allocator. Provision using real block reservations and verify the target filesystem's allocation/quota semantics at startup. Refuse effect admission on unsupported filesystems, missing quota/preallocation guarantees, changed device identity, or insufficient tokens. A lower reserve is feasible only after introducing enforced lower checkpoint/proof/audit bounds and recomputing the worst-case database growth; it cannot be inferred from current workflow-count limits.
capacityDesignProposal.sqliteAndCowPitfalls: WAL auto-checkpointing and WAL recycling are not reserves: terminal writes and checkpoints may need both WAL and main-database blocks, and a reset/reused WAL can grow. Sparse truncate/fallocate semantics and statfs watermarks are insufficient unless the exact filesystem and quota honor a real reservation. Copy-on-write snapshots or overlay filesystems can allocate copy-up blocks or metadata late; fail closed unless their reservation behavior is proven. Do not let an unanchored sidecar stand in for protected-root authentication; any emergency slot lane must be bound into the root's authenticated recovery protocol.
capacityDesignProposal.nextValidation: Measure/derive worst-case deltas for audit append, owner transaction/WAL/checkpoint and root CAS at enforced serialized maxima on each declared filesystem; test token persistence, contention, crash retention, exhaustion-before-effect rejection, and release only after all three durable records agree.
